definitions.gloss: coming and going; traffic; passage of people
definitions.explanation: The movement of people or vehicles back and forth along a route. Refers to the flow of traffic or pedestrians.
A road or street where people pass through, especially a public road in a town. A somewhat traditional or literary word for street.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}の{往来|おうらい}が{激|はげ}しい。
この{通|とお}りは{車|くるま}の{往来|おうらい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This street has a lot of vehicle traffic.

examples.japanese: {工事中|こうじちゅう}のため、{歩行者|ほこうしゃ}の{往来|おうらい}が{制限|せいげん}されている。
examples.english: Pedestrian traffic is restricted due to construction.

examples.japanese: {往来|おうらい}で{遊|あそ}んではいけない。
examples.english: You must not play in the street.

examples.japanese: {往来|おうらい}に{面|めん}した{店|みせ}は{目立|めだ}つ。
examples.english: A shop facing the street stands out.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}はこの{往来|おうらい}に{沿|そ}って{多|おお}くの{商家|しょうか}が{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: In the past, many merchant houses lined this street.

notes:
USAGE:
{往来|おうらい} combines {往|おう} (going) and {来|らい} (coming). It can function as a noun or as a suru verb ({往来|おうらい}する = to come and go). Sense 2 (street) has a somewhat old-fashioned feel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}の{往来|おうらい} (foot traffic)
- {車|くるま}の{往来|おうらい} (vehicle traffic)
- {往来|おうらい}が{激|はげ}しい (heavy traffic)
- {往来|おうらい}に{面|めん}する (to face the street)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{交通|こうつう} is the standard modern word for traffic and transportation. {往来|おうらい} has a more traditional feel and specifically emphasizes the back-and-forth movement of people.
